normalizations.policy: Every replacement below is applied identically by tests/ag3-slot-lock-reference.mjs (reference side) and tests/ag3_slot_lock.rs (native side) before comparison. Nothing else is rewritten: every byte outside these exact substitutions is compared, so a wrong or unexpected value still fails. The menu reference has no value normalization; only the injected entropy below is fixed.

items.where: lease snapshots, for an ownerId string exactly equal to the ownerId returned by the acquire that created the case
items.why: Each acquisition mints a random owner id, and renewal rewrites it. Only that case's exact captured owner is replaced; a corrupt or foreign owner id is compared verbatim.
The successor lease's random owner id is replaced unconditionally after acquisition succeeds; its expiresAt is compared exactly, and the child, contender and leftover entries remain exact.
The message embeds the per-case private mkdtemp path. Each side replaces only its own case scratch root with the same token; the rest of the message, including the error name, is compared unchanged.

The pinned slot writes a marker derived from the expected auth path. Both sides replace only that exact digest, so the fixture never contains the temporary path and any other text, including malformed markers, is compared verbatim.

items.where: credential-slot snapshot when a parent component was replaced by a regular file
items.native: tests/ag3_slot_lock.rs: ErrorKind::NotFound or raw_os_error() == ENOTDIR -> Value::Null
items.why: Linux reports ENOTDIR rather than ENOENT when an ancestor is a file. Both sides map only those two absence errors to absent and panic or throw on every other error, so a real permission or IO failure is not hidden.

items.where: menu item ids in the reference walk
items.why: Item ids are salted with one 16-byte draw. Only that draw is fixed; menu text, ordering, uiTrace, calls and notifications are compared without normalization.

compared: Renewable lease corrupt owner identity: non-string ownerId, boolean/array/object/hex/padded/negative/zero expiresAt, extra fields, symlink and legacy-directory owners
Eviction-marker corruption: a regular-file marker, a malformed owner file, a foreign owner at fresh and stale ages
Lease loss and compromise: assert and renewal against a malformed, directory-replaced or removed lease, and a marker stolen during renewal or release
Cancellation before commit: a lease destroyed while held is not revived, and a released lease is not removed when its marker was stolen

Credential slot: a second instance restores or refuses after a foreign login, an interrupted auth or stash rename stays recoverable, and a stash parent replaced by a file refuses with the original io error
Competing processes: a real child process holds the pinned lease, a contender is refused, the child releases, and a successor acquires the freed path
Every deterministic /antigravity walk: exact select/confirm/notify UI trace, callback order, confirmation true/false, cancellation at the root, section, entry and item levels, and refusal projection
Exact informational and error notification strings for use/decline/accept/use-vault/use-local/forget/request-access

approvedException.behavior: The original Node 24 body read stays pending after an idle timeout or cancellation; the native transport returns the timeout/cancellation error and releases its request.

notTested: The bare Rust credential slot intentionally has no inner Pi mkdir/mtime lock: native rpi runs it under the host credentialStoreLock. Bare-slot scenarios that would trip that lock (for example a read-only auth directory) are therefore not differentially comparable and are excluded.

A lease write failure that propagates a raw filesystem error (for example a read-only lock directory) is not captured: the pinned lock rejects with a raw Node error code while the native port maps it to a private failure, so the error shapes are not equal without an unapproved normalization. Slot write failures are covered instead (a stash parent replaced by a file, and the existing fsync fixture).
The loaded host binary used for the ignored test and the native menu script was built from a sibling host lane's target directory; rebuilding the host is outside this lane.
Competing-process contention is captured for the pinned renewable lease. Cross-process contention at the native credentialStoreLock boundary (two host processes) is not scripted here.
macOS and Windows execution was not performed; the slot and lease code cross-checks on Rust 1.78 but only Linux ran.
Live vault enrollment, custody send and inference are out of scope and were not exercised.
